newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow Australian stocks slide to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Slow Australian stocks slide to lower close.

text.p: The Australian share market drifted to close just lower on Monday as traders remained indecisive and uninterested ahead of further Wall Street moves and the much-awaited Wallis report into the financial system.
The All Ordinaries index eased 3.5 points to 2,366.0.
After spending the early part of the day in modestly firmer territory, the lack of interest told in the afternoon session as several leaders slipped into the red.
"It's been a very quiet day," said dealer Scott Healey of Brisbane-based brokerage Wilson HTM, suggesting that the next few days may be similar as investors looked for leads.
"It has been real sit on the fence type of stuff and you could see a couple of days of this."
The eagerly awaited Wallis report, expected sometime this week, underpinned early interest in the bank sector but this group also faded in the afternoon.
The major banks finished mixed. Sector leader National Australia Bank lost 0.5 percent to A$15.54 (US$12.05) albeit on exceptionally thin volume.

In the regionals, shares in takeover target Bank of Melbourne lost about one percent to A$9.38 as traders considered the political and regulatory hurdles Westpac's A$9.75 per share bid had yet to overcome.

Newspaper group John Fairfax topped turnover, with 24.54 million shares traded, the bulk of it in one line of 22.75 million shares specialled through Merrill Lynch at a price of A$2.99 per share. Its shares closed down two cents at A$3.00.
Falls shaded rises by a whisker, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
